title: Check yourself: CI, code review and workflows triggered by repository events

questions.stem: A workflow starts a runner whenever anyone posts anything, and the bill follows the volume. Which line fixes it?

options.text: A longer `timeout-minutes` value on the job that runs the step
options.says: Ruled out because the timeout bounds one run and does not stop runs from starting: the page lists it with "workflow-level timeouts to avoid runaway jobs".

options.text: An `if` on the job that tests the comment body for `@claude`
options.says: The page says "Without the `if`, a runner starts for every comment in the repository", and the guard is `if: contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')`.

options.text: A larger `--max-turns` value in the arguments of the action step
options.says: Ruled out because "Set `--max-turns` in `claude_args` to limit iterations", which acts inside a run and does not stop one from starting.

options.text: A write permission on the contents of the repository for the job
options.says: Ruled out because write access is a permission and not a trigger filter, and the page says "Grant the least a job needs".

questions.stem: A review job should inspect the code and post findings. Which permission set fits?

options.text: Write on the contents, with scopes for comments and authentication
options.says: Ruled out because "A job that implements changes needs `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`", and a review only reads, so the extra write access lets a compromised run change the repository.

options.text: No access to the contents, with scopes for comments and authentication
options.says: Ruled out because "A job that only reviews needs `contents: read`", so some access to the code is required.

options.text: Read on the contents alone, with nothing else granted to the job
options.says: Ruled out because the review example includes `id-token: write`, which the documentation calls "required for the Claude Code GitHub Action's default GitHub App authentication".

options.text: Read on the contents, with scopes for comments and authentication
options.says: The page says "A job that only reviews needs `contents: read`", and the review example reads pull requests and issues as well, and has the `id-token: write` permission for authentication.

questions.stem: Code Review's findings are posted on a pull request, and a team wants them to hold up the merge button. What does the review's check run do?

options.text: It fails whenever a finding is rated important, so merging stops
options.says: Ruled out because the check run "always completes with a neutral conclusion", so no rating makes it fail.

options.text: It ends neutral every time, so nothing waits on it
options.says: The page says "The check run always completes with a neutral conclusion so it never blocks merging through branch protection rules."

options.text: It approves the pull request, so a clean review lifts any block
options.says: Ruled out because findings "don't approve or block your PR", so a clean review approves nothing either.

options.text: It requests changes from the author, so each finding must be fixed
options.says: Ruled out because findings are posted "as inline comments", and the page says "So it advises, and a person merges."
